newsitem.title: UK: Czarnikow sees similar 1997/98 European beet area.
newsitem.headline: Czarnikow sees similar 1997/98 European beet area.

text.p: Sugar beet sowing areas across Europe are expected to be broadly similar for the 1997/98 crop as for the previous season, Czarnikow Sugar said in its latest report published on Thursday.
France and Germany, the EU's two largest producers, would see slight area increases while the Belgian area would be a fractional one percent lower than in 1996/97.
Areas in Britain, Scandinavia and the Netherlands would be similar, it said. Russia's beet area was officially forecast to rise slightly for the second season running.

In Italy the price relationship between cereals and sugar beet had reversed from last season, when higher prices for alternative crops prompted farmers to switch out of beet and caused the sowing area to fall.
This season the Italian area would recover from 248,000 hectares to a maximum 280,000 hecatres, it said.

"Overall changes are not expected to be more than nominal amounts except in one or two isolated cases and the key factor for the initial stages of the season will be the weather," the Czarnikow report said.
"Conditions must be fair enough to allow machinery to work the fields and then remain mild to encourage early germination. Some rain, once the crop is in the ground, would also be welcome," it added.
Europe's total beet area totalled 6.05 million hectares in 1996/97, Czarnikow said.
This was split between 2.61 million for the former Soviet Union, 860,000 for the rest of eastern Europe, 2.02 million for the European Union (EU) and 550,000 for other west European countries.
